description: Wrapper around Robin Schmidt's open303, a monophonic 303-style bass voice with a built-in acid sequencer pattern

params.text: Blends the oscillator from a saw at 0 to a square at 1
Sets the tuning reference, 400Hz to 480Hz, with A at 440Hz by default
Sets the filter cutoff, held at 261.63Hz over the lower half of the travel and climbing ten octaves above that over the upper half
Sets the filter resonance, 0 to 100 percent
Sets how much of the envelope is applied to the filter cutoff, 0 to 100 percent
Sets the decay time of the filter envelope, 200ms to 2 seconds
Sets how much louder and brighter an accented step is than an unaccented one, 0 to 100 percent
Picks the mode of the 303 filter model
Runs the built-in acid sequencer pattern in place of notes arriving at the gate input

inputs.text: Sets the pitch of the note, 0V giving middle C, read at the moment the gate opens
A rising edge starts a note, which ends when the voltage falls below 0.5V
Sets how hard the note is struck, 0V to 10V covering the MIDI velocity range, with 100 used while the jack is empty
Shifts the saw-to-square blend, a tenth of a volt covering the whole of it
Raises the tuning reference by 3Hz per volt
Raises the filter cutoff by an octave per volt
Raises the resonance by 10 percent per volt
Raises the envelope amount by 10 percent per volt
Lengthens the filter envelope decay by 400ms per volt
Raises the accent amount by 10 percent per volt
Raises the output level by a thirtieth of a decibel per volt
Nothing in the module reads this jack; the filter model is picked by the knob above it alone

outputs.text: The voice, one channel however many channels arrive at the gate input

notes: nothing sounds until a gate arrives at the gate input, or the run seq switch is turned on to play the built-in pattern.
